name: Toshiba NAND flash memory
description: An electrically erasable nonvolatile semiconductor memory organized using a NAND-structured cell array.

date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Masuoka and colleagues described NAND-structured flash memory at the 1987 International Electron Devices Meeting.

contributions.resource: Toshiba’s camera division supported the broader NAND project.

evidence.supports: CHM dates the NAND description to 1987 and identifies Toshiba camera-division funding.

events.caveats: Conference paper and funding are not proof of commercial availability in 1987.

evidence.supports: CHM dates the NAND description to 1987 and identifies Toshiba camera-division funding.
The indexed abstract identifies the 1987 four-author paper.

date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Toshiba began production of 16-megabit NAND flash chips.

evidence.supports: CHM dates production of 16-Mbit NAND to 1992.

date.label: by 23 May 2005
date.basis: Date of report describing use; image capture date unspecified.

events.statement: An NTSB study recovered image files from a SmartMedia card used in an Olympus digital camera.

evidence.supports: Reports the camera and nine recovered images on its card.
Connects SmartMedia with expansion of NAND flash memory and digital-camera storage.

events.caveats: A single documented use; the source does not establish market share, earliest consumer use, or identity of a particular NAND chip.
events.scope: Study report date, not necessarily the date the images were taken.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event establishing this scoped achievement; it is not a claim of global priority.

places.note: Research organization Toshiba was based in Japan; presentation occurred in Washington.

measures.subject: 1992 NAND flash chips
measures.conditions: CHM retrospective; capacity, not quantity sold.

caveats: Electrically erasable and flash memories predated NAND. The source dates this implementation and does not establish the first consumer product. SmartMedia camera use is evidenced in a later case, not established as the first consumer use.

research.note: New source-backed draft; independent review pending. Independent reader checked the conference abstract and CHM’s funding and 1992 production account; chip capacity is not sales. Independent reader checked the 2005 NTSB SmartMedia case and Kioxia’s general account; they do not identify the individual chip or establish market share.
